query: What open-response signals predict low learning satisfaction?

per_column.name: instructional_pacing_issue
per_column.rationale: Pacing (too_fast/too_slow) is a plausible driver of low satisfaction and gives a real grouping axis. Values match evidence: ED-0001 'three problems ahead' -> too_fast, ED-0004 self-paced -> appropriate. Heavily skewed to not_present but that is honest silence, not penalized.

per_column.name: asynchronous_content_benefit
per_column.rationale: Distinguishing reusable/rewatchable vs livestream_only is a useful modality axis. ED-0004 pause/rewatch -> reusable is well grounded. However ED-0005 -> livestream_only is a somewhat confident inference from 'discussion' with no explicit format cue, and the near-absence of not_present suggests over-assignment where text is silent.

per_column.name: hands_on_or_lab_gap
per_column.rationale: Lab/hands-on gap is a meaningful axis for subjects that suffer remotely. ED-0002 kitchen-chemistry -> partial_simulation_support is reasonable. Mostly not_applicable, which is honest for silent rows.

per_column.name: peer_interaction_quality
per_column.rationale: Peer interaction is a strong candidate predictor and well categorized. ED-0003 'zero peer interaction' -> isolated_individual, ED-0005 'cameras off... silent' -> cameras_muted_silent are precise, faithful readings.

per_column.name: teacher_feedback_responsiveness
per_column.rationale: Feedback responsiveness is a plausible satisfaction driver. ED-0003 'teacher can't tell when she's lost' -> no_interaction is sound. Values track the text; many not_present is honest.

per_column.name: subject_remote_format_fit
per_column.rationale: The axis is useful, but the label 'excellent_fit_discussion_based' vs 'poor_fit_hands_on_dependent' conflates fit judgment with format type and is over-asserted. ED-0002 (chemistry labs) -> excellent_fit_discussion_based contradicts the hands-on nature; ED-0004 (history) mapped to a discussion label though respondent praised recorded lectures. Confident specifics not clearly warranted.

per_column.name: emotional_affect_during_class
per_column.rationale: Emotional affect is more than a bare sentiment flag (graded categories incl. distressed_crying) and offers analytic leverage. ED-0003 'cries' -> distressed_crying, ED-0001 frustration -> anxious_frustrated are faithful.

per_column.name: curiosity_and_intrinsic_motivation_trajectory
per_column.rationale: Motivation trajectory is a useful axis but risks restating emotional_affect, and 'trajectory' asserts change over time that many single responses do not support. ED-0004/ED-0002 growth is warranted, but ED-0001/ED-0003 -> declining_lost_passion infers a trajectory from a snapshot of dissatisfaction, an over-confident temporal claim.

judge.rationale: The added columns supply several genuinely distinct axes (pacing, peer interaction, feedback, affect, hands-on gap) that are well suited to predicting low learning satisfaction from open responses, and most values are faithful, well-categorized readings of the source text with honest not_present/not_applicable handling for silent rows. Two columns lose points on groundedness: subject_remote_format_fit over-asserts a fit judgment that sometimes contradicts the text (chemistry labs labeled discussion-based), and the curiosity/motivation 'trajectory' column infers directional change from snapshot responses and partly restates emotional affect. Overall a solid, mostly grounded and analytically useful set.
